passage: The photocopy shop outside the tehsil office in Shahabad was hot by noon, and so was the argument. Devika had found the cash box two hundred short again, and Wasim had just used the word "careless" about her accounts. Her voice rose. His did too. Then Wasim stopped, put both hands flat on the counter, and said, "I'm too angry to say anything useful. Give me one hour. I'll be back at one o'clock and we'll finish this." He walked to the canal bank and sat under the peepal tree. Devika watched him go, arms folded, half expecting him to disappear till night the way her uncle always did. At five to one, his cycle bell rang outside. He came in with two cups of tea.

qa.q: Where did Wasim go during the hour?
qa.a: He walked to the canal bank and sat under the peepal tree.

qa.q: How did Devika feel as she watched Wasim walk out?
qa.a: She felt wary and still angry, arms folded, half expecting him to disappear till night the way her uncle always did.

qa.q: What made Wasim's pause work instead of feeling like storming off?
qa.a: He named his anger, gave a clear return time, and came back at five to one, even bringing tea.

qa.q: What might Wasim have been going through as he sat under the peepal tree?
qa.a: Wasim was too angry to say anything useful, so he used the hour by the canal to calm down before coming back to finish the talk.

grounding: Shows a young man calling a stated time-out when too angry to talk well and coming back when he said he would.

passage: The argument in the tiny Valencia flat began over the heating bill and slid quickly into everything else. Beatriz was pacing; Ivan felt his jaw lock and heard himself about to say something about her mother. He stopped. "Bea, I'm too angry to talk well. Can we pick this up in an hour? Seven o'clock. I'm just going for a walk." She threw up her hands. "Great, just leave." "I'm coming back. Seven." He went down to the seafront and walked until his shoulders dropped. At six fifty-five, the key turned in the lock. He had two oranges from the corner shop and a calmer voice. Beatriz, who had spent the hour rehearsing how abandoned she felt, found she didn't need the speech.

qa.q: At what time did the key turn in the lock?
qa.a: The key turned in the lock at six fifty-five.

qa.q: What was Ivan worried he was about to say?
qa.a: He felt his jaw lock and sensed he was about to say something about Beatriz's mother, which he knew would do damage.

qa.q: Why did the stated return time matter so much here?
qa.a: Beatriz first heard the break as "just leave"; saying "seven" and keeping it turned a walkout into a pause she could trust.

qa.q: What was the hour like for Beatriz?
qa.a: She spent it feeling abandoned and rehearsing a speech, but his early return meant she no longer needed it.

grounding: Shows a partner asking for an hour's pause with a set return time and keeping it, so the break does not read as punishment.
